translation_direction: ru → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete Russian electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Tolstoy’s calm, concrete late style, the cold irony of the court chapters and the plain respect for the mountain people are kept in sober literary Vietnamese with no explanatory padding; French stays French.
decisions.rationale: The effect depends on the facts being allowed to speak.

decisions.decision: The Russian text comes from Wikisource because the backlog entry named no text; it is translated directly from the Russian.
decisions.rationale: Translation from the original, not from an English or other version.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: ‘Пасынок’ (Bulka, the wife’s son) was rendered as Vorontsov’s own stepson in a way that reversed the relation; now ‘con riêng của vợ Vorontsov’, consistent with ‘cha dượng’.
‘Вышел к русским’ (Hadji Murat’s defection) was rendered ‘ra đầu hàng’ / ‘ra hàng’, turning defection into surrender, in units 456, 477 and 546; now ‘sang phía người Nga’.
‘Лихорадочное состояние’ (a feverish, agitated state) was rendered as malaria; corrected.
‘Шурин’ (the empress’s brother, the Prussian king) was rendered ‘người anh rể’ (a sister’s husband), in units 625 and 636; now ‘anh vợ’.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.rationale: Latin transcription of the hero’s name.

glossary.draft_rendering: cây kế … Tatar … cây kế bị giẫm nát giữa cánh đồng vừa cày
glossary.rationale: The image of chapter I returns in the last line.

witness_decision: Selected the Russian Wikisource transcription of Хаджи-Мурат (written 1896–1904, first published posthumously in 1912), which cites the 1912 Berlin edition and the 1983 Soviet 22-volume edition as its sources; the project did not collate it with a printed edition.

unresolved_questions.explanation: ‘Сдался’ is rendered ‘đầu hàng’, a wording the book avoids for Hadji Murat’s defection.
The masked word is rendered ‘đ...n’, which reads as an arbitrary fragment.
Marya Vasilyevna’s garbled proverb reads as nonsense.
Hadji Murat’s broken Russian is rendered as correct Vietnamese.

title_review.rationale: The title is the hero’s name in Latin letters; no earlier Vietnamese title was checked.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: The opening: the narrator, returning home across the fields, gathers a bouquet and sees the thistle.
The last unit: the crushed thistle among the ploughed field recalls Hadji Murat’s death.
